Since I am certain that Chordify also does not have an office in Chicago, or collect more than $100,000 annually from customers in Chicago, they are not subject to any local taxes, and I find it hard to believe that they are forwarding this “Tax” to the city, so it seems a little bit like fraud, or something put in by an overzealous legal counsel. Progression displays and PDFs, not ready for prime time. PDFs and in-app diagrams desperately need reworking. If someone were to put these displays and/or lead sheets (PDFs) in front of any serious musician, they’d either laugh at derisively while struggling to keep their place, or they would walk out of the session. 

Here’s why: standard lead sheets are four measures across. This, of course is owing to the fact that the majority of popular music sections are divisible by four (8, 12, 16, 32 bars). When this app renders a PDF that is a ludicrous 11 bars across the page, it is darn near impossible to use for either practice or rehearsal. I do get that section, navigation, and dynamic markers would be extremely challenging (programming wise), but a standard four bars across, perhaps in a larger font, seems within reach, if not trivial.

Other parts of the app are very helpful, but I’m sure I am not the only musician who finds the format of the progressions cumbersome and frustrating.

The only other reservation I have so far, is that the analysis of songs that I’ve input so far don’t seem to recognize or honor slash chords. As a bass player who utilizes a fair bit of voice leading, I still have to rely solely on my ear to suss out what’s happening. I would do this anyway, so it’s a smaller concern by far then the formatting issue cited above.

Thanks for your consideration.

reviews.text: Are these reviews for a different app?. This is the worst app I’ve used for guitar chords in terms of trying to nickel and dime the user. Constant popups and other asks for a premium subscription while very poorly communicating the advantages of paying. Other reviews indicate there are vocal coaching, songwriting, and other beneficial features in this app beyond the basic functionality of giving you chords for songs. For me, I was linked to this app after repeatedly googling for the chords to a song that I had mostly figured out but felt one section I must have been playing incorrectly but couldn’t work out what the error was (I have over 20 years experience playing guitar). The links to the chords for this one (admittedly kind of obscure) song all pointed to downloading this app. For my narrower purposes the app has largely failed in most applications. Every song I look up (several of which I know *very* well just to test the app’s library) is close to , but not quite, correct. Turns out one of the features the devs are quite proud of is the software auto-detecting chords for music it can find online. The problem is this software is (again, in my limited testing) very often if not always wrong to a technical but more often even more importantly very *noticeable* degree. But the app does a terrible job communicating that this feature was used to get the progression being shown that no human musician has vetted the outcome in any way. So I fear that newer musicians will assume the info provided is correct when it’s better used as a best guess for experienced musicians that can work through the noise. Two stars for the features other reviewers seem to appreciate that I can’t even find.
